references.name: classic-front.jpg
references.observed: Complete historic seaward front actually inspected: warm ochre/pale stone facade, two cylindrical end towers with steep slate conical/curved roofs and open top lanterns, a long steep main hip/mansard roof with dormers, a central shaped clock gable, repeated rectangular and tall arched windows, pilasters/cornices and open balcony rails. Three broad glazed arched ground entrances lie between narrower end arches. The narrow strip of quay and rock seawall is context, not part of the passenger building. Exact inscriptions, railway logo, sculptural reliefs and banners are not copied.

references.name: station-2024.jpg
references.observed: 2024 whole front/long-side view actually inspected. Steep gray slate main roof and corner conical roofs/lanterns are visible during scaffolding/restoration. A long side wing has repeated arched ground openings, several upper window levels and a dense row of small roof dormers, with larger shaped roof gables near its ends. The source model should represent the complete permanent architectural exterior; temporary scaffolding, perimeter banners/fences and the large roof logo are excluded. Hidden courtyard/rear opening inventory remains approximate.

note: Two ordinary public front/side photographs, current standard PMTiles and standard viewer terrain only. Pictures remain local observation references, not redistributed textures. No bespoke archival, survey or per-building terrain research.
